# Maximum Number of Points from Grid Queries

## Problem

You receive an integer matrix named `grid` (`int[][]`) along with an integer array called `queries` (`int[]`). Begin at the upper-left position and travel one step at a time in any of the four cardinal directions.

For every threshold `q`, determine the number of cells reachable from that starting position when every visited cell must contain a value smaller than `q`. Produce these counts in the same sequence as the input queries.

## Examples

Example 1:

Input: `grid = [[2,4,6],[3,8,9],[5,7,1]], queries = [6,9,3]`

Output: `[4,8,1]`

Explanation: With thresholds `6`, `9`, and `3`, the reachable-cell totals are `4`, `8`, and `1`, respectively, because only cells with values strictly below each threshold may be used.

## Constraints

* `2 <= grid.length, grid[i].length <= 1000`
* `1 <= queries.length <= 10^4`
* `1 <= grid[i][j], queries[i] <= 10^6`

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Process queries in increasing order, as the threshold rises, more cells become reachable.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a min-heap to expand from the start, always visiting the smallest cell value first, and a visited set.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Sort queries, then for each query expand all cells with value less than the query threshold, updating the count.

</details>
